newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Costello wants more competition in payments system.
newsitem.headline: Costello wants more competition in payments system.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday he wanted more competition in the payments and settlements system, which is currently limited to just banks and some credit unions.
Insurance groups, telecommunications companies and others have said they should be allowed access to the payments system.
The Wallis Financial System Inquiry recommended the payments system be extended to allow building societies, credit unions and their associates to issue cheques in their own names.

It recommended other financial institutions should be allowed to issue cheques in agency arrangements with deposit taking institutions or their associates, subject to the approval of a new body created to monitor the payments system.
This new body would be called Payments Systems Board (PSB) and be formed within the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), but that the PSB board would be independent of the RBA.
The PSB replaces the Australian Payments System Council, which would be disbanded, Wallis recommended.
